newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INTERVIEW - NKF CEO says exports growing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - NKF CEO says exports growing.

text.p: Telecommunications and energy cable maker NKF Holding NV said on Wednesday its export markets were growing "significantly" because of the company's ability to offer added value to its product range.
In 1995 NKF made a net profit of 40.5 million guilders ($23.7 million) on turnover of 1.2 billion guilders, with some 24 percent of the turnover generated outside of NKF's "home" markets.
"They (exports) will be significantly higher than 24 percent this year," chairman and chief executive Tonn van de Laar said in an interview, declining to add financial detail.

"One of the biggest and fastest growers is cables for mobile telephony infrastructure. They are very unusual cables, which look totally different to the classical telecommunications cables," said Van der Laar.
"That product has so much added value, it's so complex to make, has so many sophisticated properties, (and) it's really worthwhile exporting around the world," he said.
Transporting and installing cable in defined projects and taking part in turn-key projects for major operators were other ways of adding value.

"Optical fibre cable as such is always the same, but if you're able not only to bury it but also to install it in overhead powerlines, then you have added value which allows you to get a better margin," said Van de Laar.
Van de Laar said for future stability NKF had to look abroad, where there could be opportunities to cash in on the worldwide liberalisation in power and telecoms industries.
"If you want to be stable and not vulnerable to the decisions of one customer you have to go to more customers which automatically means you have to go international," he said.

"For us an important market is in the east bloc where we are building up relationships with specific customers to deliver them the same kind of services we're delivering here in western Europe. A big part of the growth has come from that," he added.

Van de Laar expressed satisfaction with NKF's operating margin in 1995 of 5.83 percent and its 15.42 percent return on equity. "If you look to the major players in our industry, some of our big competitors are in red figures," he said.

He added that continuing liberalisation of power and telecoms industries should provide new opportunities, although more exotic possibilities could exist in the new millennium with the explosion of telecoms technology and anticipated proliferation of traffic management schemes.

"Telecom operators will change from companies who are technology driven, whose traditional activity was to build, maintain and exploit a network, they will become operators and nothing but operators," said Van de Laar. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000 ($ = 1.711 Dutch Guilders)
